name: Single-Arm Cable High Row with Rotation
description: The single-arm cable high row with rotation pulls from a high cable pulley with one hand while adding a torso rotation at peak contraction toward the working side. The rotation engages the obliques and thoracic rotators alongside the standard lat and upper back muscles, training the pulling pattern in a more athletically functional context that mirrors rotational sport movements.

execution.starting_position: Stand side-on to a high cable pulley. Grasp the handle with the near hand, arm extended upward toward the pulley. Feet staggered or parallel at shoulder width.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the cable to the highest available position. Stand far enough from the stack to achieve full arm extension at the starting position.
steps: Step 1: Begin with arm extended toward the high pulley.
Step 2: Pull the cable handle toward the hip or lower ribcage, driving the elbow down.
Step 3: At peak contraction, rotate the torso toward the working side.
Step 4: Hold 1 second at peak rotation.
Step 5: Reverse the motion — unwind the torso then return the arm — to full extension.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the pull and rotation. Inhale on the return.
common_mistakes: Rotating before the pull completes — the row and rotation should sequence, not co-occur
Using momentum from the rotation to assist the pull — the lat should drive the pull
safety_considerations: Thoracic rotation under load can stress spinal structures — keep loads moderate
Avoid if experiencing thoracic or lumbar spine pain
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full arm extension to full torso rotation at peak contraction.
coaching_cues: Drive the elbow to the hip before the torso turns
Control the reverse sequence on the way back
